What your child's eye test misses

A school vision screening that comes back normal doesn't always mean everything is fine. These tests typically check whether a child can read letters on a chart at a distance. But they miss quite a bit.

Conditions like convergence insufficiency (where both eyes struggle to work together at close range) rarely show up on a standard chart test. Yet they can cause a child to skip lines while reading, get headaches after homework, or lose focus well before others in the class do. As an eye specialist in Malad, Dr. Archana Gotecha checks binocular function, near vision coordination and eye movement control as part of a full paediatric eye evaluation.

The clinic is at Dr. Chhabildas Sanghvi Eye Hospital on S.V. Road, Malad West. If your child reads slowly or avoids close work, it may be worth looking a little deeper than the school test did.

Diabetic Eye Check: Don't Skip It

If you have diabetes, your eyes can start changing before your vision does. That's the part most people miss. Blood sugar fluctuations affect the tiny vessels inside the retina, often silently, long before any blurring or discomfort shows up.

A dilated eye exam done specifically for diabetic patients looks at the retinal vessels for early signs of diabetic retinopathy, macular swelling and optic nerve health. Dr. Archana Gotecha, with over 21 years of experience in complete eye care at her Malad West clinic, recommends this check at least once a year for anyone managing diabetes, even if your sight feels fine right now.

The clinic is at Dr. Chhabildas Sanghvi Eye Hospital on S.V. Road, Malad West. If diabetes runs in your family or you've been managing it for a few years, it's worth scheduling a proper retinal review soon.

What your retina reveals about your health

Most people think an eye check is only about glasses. But the retina at the back of your eye is one of the few places in the body where blood vessels can be seen directly, without any cut or scan. Changes there often show up before you feel anything.

Dr. Archana Gotecha has MBBS, DOMS, FCPS and DNB in Ophthalmology, along with 21 years of practice. A retinal examination as part of a comprehensive eye check-up in Malad West looks at the optic nerve, macular health and vascular patterns that a standard vision test simply doesn't reach.

The clinic is at Dr. Chhabildas Sanghvi Eye Hospital on S.V. Road, Malad West. If it's been a while since your last full eye examination, it may be worth scheduling one soon.

What cataract surgery prep really involves

Many people assume cataract surgery is something you only do when you can barely see. So they wait until vision gets bad enough to feel urgent. But by that point, the clouding has often made daily tasks harder for longer than necessary, and the eye itself takes more work to recover from a dense cataract than a moderate one.

The pre-surgical assessment for cataract eye surgery in Malad West involves biometry measurements to calculate the exact lens power needed for your eye. That calculation is specific to each person and affects how clearly you see after surgery. Getting it right matters as much as the procedure itself.

Dr. Archana Gotecha consults at Dr. Chhabildas Sanghvi Eye Hospital on S.V. Road, Malad West, easy to reach from Kandivali and Goregaon. If someone in your family has been putting off a cataract evaluation, it may be worth coming in sooner rather than waiting for vision to get worse.

LASIK isn't the only option

Glasses and contact lenses aren't the only route out of blurry vision. A lot of people don't realise there are multiple surgical options available now, and LASIK is just one of them. The right choice depends on your corneal thickness, prescription strength and lifestyle.

Vitreoretinal surgery, LASIK and corneal treatments are all offered here, but the starting point is always a proper evaluation of what your eye can support. For anyone exploring LASIK in Malad West, the pre-assessment looks at corneal maps, pupil size and tear film health before any recommendation is made. So the process itself answers the question.

Dr. Archana Gotecha consults at Dr. Chhabildas Sanghvi Eye Hospital on S.V. Road, Malad West. If you've been on the fence about vision correction, it's worth sitting down and finding out what your options actually are.

When dry eyes need more than drops

Itchy, watery eyes that keep coming back even after using lubricating drops are easy to shrug off. But persistent dryness that doesn't settle is worth looking at more closely, because the cause isn't always the same for everyone.

Dry eye has different types, and the right treatment depends on whether the problem is with tear production, tear quality or lid gland function. Dr. Archana Gotecha assesses dry eye as part of general eye care in Malad West, checking the tear film and ocular surface properly rather than assuming drops alone will fix it.

The clinic is at Dr. Chhabildas Sanghvi Eye Hospital on S.V. Road in Malad West, reachable from Kandivali and Goregaon. If lubricating drops have stopped helping, it may be time to find out what's actually behind it.

What happens during a squint check

A child squinting or tilting their head to see clearly is easy to brush off as a habit. But these small adjustments often mean the eyes aren't working together the way they should, and the earlier it gets picked up, the more the brain can be retrained.

A squint correction evaluation checks eye alignment, muscle balance and how well both eyes coordinate for clear vision. Dr. Archana Gotecha, an ophthalmologist in Malad West with 21 years of experience, assesses both children and adults, since squint doesn't disappear on its own without the right intervention.

The clinic is at Dr. Chhabildas Sanghvi Eye Hospital on S.V. Road, Malad West, easy to reach from Kandivali and Goregaon. If you've noticed a turn or a tilt that keeps coming back, it's worth getting checked properly.

What a corneal topography shows

Dry, gritty eyes and light sensitivity are easy to dismiss as screen fatigue or dust. But sometimes the surface of the cornea itself is the source, and that's something only a proper slit-lamp and corneal assessment can pick up, not a basic glasses check.

Corneal topography maps the exact curvature and surface irregularities of your eye. It picks up early keratoconus, post-surgical changes and surface dryness patterns that a standard eye test would miss entirely. For anyone exploring LASIK treatment in Malad West, this mapping is part of the pre-surgical work, but it's useful for non-surgical patients too.

Dr. Archana Gotecha consults at Dr. Chhabildas Sanghvi Eye Hospital, right on S.V. Road in Malad West, easy to reach from Kandivali and Goregaon. If persistent eye discomfort hasn't had a clear answer yet, ask about a corneal evaluation at your next visit.

What DNB in Ophthalmology means for you

Most people check a doctor's years of experience and leave it at that. Fewer look at what the qualifications behind the name actually mean, and that gap can matter when you're deciding who to trust with something as specific as your vision.

DNB in Ophthalmology is a postgraduate surgical qualification awarded after rigorous theory and clinical examinations. It sits alongside FCPS and DOMS as a specialist credential, not just a general medical degree. Dr. Archana Gotecha holds all three, plus MBBS, which means 21 years of practice built on a foundation that covered cataract surgery, squint correction, vitreoretinal work and corneal care from the beginning.

Cataract Surgery Myths Worth Knowing

Many people believe cataracts only affect the very old, or that once vision starts clouding you simply have to live with it until things get bad enough. Neither is quite right. Cataracts can develop in your 40s or 50s, and waiting too long can actually make the surgery more complex, not less.

Cataract eye surgery in Malad West today is a day procedure. Most patients are home the same afternoon. The clouded natural lens is removed and replaced with a clear intraocular lens, and the improvement in sharpness is often noticeable within a day or two of healing.
